meta.note: Specific models, priced at anchor years rather than annually. An anchor is a year I have an actual view on; the app draws markers at anchors and interpolates between them, so the interpolation is never mistaken for data. CAGR is computed endpoint-to-endpoint from anchors only.

kinds.retail: Boutique list price. Rising retail is what the object COSTS you, not what you earn — benchmarked against CPI.
kinds.resale: Secondary-market or auction value. This is the investment question — benchmarked against the S&P 500.

items.name: Rolex Daytona
items.blurb: The hype watch of the 2010s. Launched at $12,400 retail and never sold at retail.
items.source: Secondary-market asking prices; the 2021-22 peak and subsequent fall are widely reported
items.caveat: Anyone who actually paid retail did far better than this line — but waitlists meant almost nobody could.

items.name: Rolex Submariner Date
items.blurb: What Rolex charges at the counter.
items.caveat: List price, not what you could actually buy one for.

items.name: Rolex Submariner Date
items.blurb: The same watch on the grey market — the gap over list is the whole story.
items.caveat: Grey-market pricing is thin and dealer-quoted; spreads are wide.

items.name: Patek Philippe Nautilus
items.blurb: The most extreme watch bubble on record. Retail was about $34,900 when Patek discontinued it in 2021.
items.caveat: The single best illustration of why the start year decides everything. Buy in 2021, lose half.

items.name: AP Royal Oak
items.blurb: The third of the steel-sports-watch trinity.
items.caveat: Reference changed mid-series (15400 to 15500 in 2019); treated as one continuous model line.

items.name: Omega Speedmaster Professional
items.blurb: The sane man's grail. Actually available at retail, which is why it never bubbled.
items.caveat: The 2021 jump reflects the new co-axial master chronometer movement — not quite like-for-like.

items.name: Hermès Birkin 30
items.blurb: The boutique price — if Hermès will sell you one, which is the catch.
items.caveat: Hermès does not publish a price list; these are widely-reported figures. Leather and hardware change the price substantially.

items.name: Hermès Birkin 30
items.blurb: The rare object that reliably resells above what the shop charged.
items.caveat: Condition, colour and hardware swing this enormously; a neutral-colour example in excellent condition is assumed.

items.name: Chanel Classic Flap
items.blurb: The most aggressive price escalation in luxury retail. Chanel raised this bag roughly sevenfold in twenty years.
items.source: Widely-reported US retail prices across repeated increases
items.caveat: The headline number of this whole project: as a COST this outran inflation about fourfold. It is only a return if you owned one and sold it.

items.name: Louis Vuitton Neverfull MM
items.blurb: The entry-level status bag, and a clean read on mass-luxury price inflation.
items.caveat: Coated canvas, not leather — it does not hold resale value the way the Hermès and Chanel entries do.

items.name: Ferrari F40
items.blurb: The poster car, and one of the best-performing physical assets of the last fifteen years.
items.caveat: Excludes maintenance, which on an F40 is not a rounding error — engine-out services run five figures.

items.name: Ferrari Testarossa
items.blurb: Worth less in 2010 than in 2005, then tripled.
items.caveat: A reminder that classic cars can sit flat or fall for a decade at a time.

items.name: Ferrari 250 GTO
items.blurb: The most valuable car in the world, and the least useful data point on this page.
items.source: Public auction results — Bonhams 2014 ($38.1M), RM Sotheby's 2018 ($48.4M), Sotheby's 2023 ($51.7M)
items.caveat: A handful of sales of non-identical cars over twenty years. The CAGR is arithmetically true and practically meaningless — n is effectively three.

items.name: Porsche 911 Carrera
items.blurb: The last air-cooled 911. The most attainable car here, and it still tripled.
items.caveat: Softened after 2023 along with most of the air-cooled market.

items.name: Lamborghini Countach
items.caveat: Early LP400s only; later QV and Anniversary cars are worth a fraction of this.

items.name: Cartier Love Bracelet
items.blurb: The default luxury gift, and partly a bet on the gold price.
items.caveat: Cartier reprices this with gold, so some of the rise is bullion rather than brand.

items.name: Van Cleef Vintage Alhambra
items.blurb: The other default, and a steeper climb than the Cartier.
items.caveat: Stone variants (onyx, mother-of-pearl, malachite) price differently; plain yellow gold is assumed.
